reviews.body:
Closes the gap in #1388: a project skill could index `<RAVEN_HOME>/config.json`. `project_skill_roots` gains a `state_home` keyword defaulting to `raven_home()` (`raven/memory_engine/skill_forge/project_skills.py:58,75`) and appends its resolved path to `guarded` (`:76`). `read_project_skills` already rejects skill dirs and `SKILL.md` targets resolving into `guarded`, so both leak sites close without editing `wiring.py`/`factory.py`; the default covers production (`:346`). Type: bug fix, security hardening. Two files, +25/-2.

Checked against origin/main with HOME and RAVEN_HOME set, driving the production default: base returns the `sk-SECRET` content, head returns `[]`, while an ordinary sibling skill is still collected. Mutations: dropping `state_home_r` from `guarded` fails the new test; inverting `_is_guarded` fails three. Both red. One survives: replacing `raven_home()` with `Path.home()/".raven"` keeps all 43 tests green yet reopens the leak, so the test does not pin the production default.

The CI red is real and blocking. `d9a72ee7a` is `fix(skill_forge): ...`; commitlint rejects `skill_forge` under `scope-enum` (this tree's scope is `memory_engine`), and the prospective squash header fails identically. The Python checkers skip the scope enum, so `pull request title` is green. Amend the commit and retitle the PR; a merge-time title edit leaves the check red.

Tests: 43 passed in `tests/test_skill_forge_project_skills.py`, 105 with the router and skill-tool neighbours; ruff clean; `check-source-language`, `check-large-files`, `check-soul-legacy`, `check-pr-body` exit 0; merge-tree against origin/main clean.

Blocking: commit message and PR title scope; no code defect found. Non-blocking: docstrings still name only `~/.agents` and agent home (`project_skills.py:3-10,62-73`); the new test passes `state_home` explicitly (`tests/test_skill_forge_project_skills.py:414`), leaving the default wiring unproven; `roots.guarded[:2]` weakens the older assertion (`:390`).

Re-review of the rewritten head 549e8b6876c4 (previous head 676bb8209f64). The prior blocking commitlint item and all three non-blocking items are fixed.

Commitlint, run by me: range 3be18b87a..HEAD exits 0, and the prospective squash header `fix(memory_engine): guard RAVEN_HOME against project skill symlinks (#1390)` also exits 0. The invalid skill_forge scope is gone.

Default-wiring pin, the critical item: `test_the_default_state_home_is_the_raven_home` (tests/test_skill_forge_project_skills.py:426) patches `project_skills_module.raven_home` (:440) and calls `project_skill_roots(workdir, agent_home=..., home=...)` with no `state_home` (:442). I re-ran mutation M3 (`raven_home()` -> `Path.home() / ".raven"`): 1 failed, 43 passed; `test_the_default_state_home_is_the_raven_home` fails at :444 with guarded[2] `.../home/.raven` != `.../repo/.raven`. M1 still fails 3 tests, M2 still fails 4.

A/B security probe through the production default path with only HOME and RAVEN_HOME set: origin/main reads 1 skill with content `{"api_key": "sk-SECRET"}`; head reads 0 skills. Docstrings now name RAVEN_HOME (project_skills.py:12, :73-76), and the weakened `guarded[:2]` is a full three-root equality at :392.

Tests: 44 passed in the target file (was 43), 106 in the four adjacent suites (was 105). ruff check and format clean. check_commit_messages, check_source_language, check_large_files, check_pr_title all exit 0. merge-tree with origin/main rc=0. CI on the new head is fully green, including commit messages and pull request title.

Non-blocking: the PR body Verification still says 33 passed; the current count is 44. Refresh it before merge.

## Windows compatibility review

Scope: full diff at `d9a72ee7aef29c9abe82808f44837e31146a625b` (base `b0dd64107e`), 2 files: `project_skill_roots` adds `RAVEN_HOME` (via `raven_home()`, `state_home` keyword for tests) to `guarded`, so `read_project_skills` rejects any skill directory or `SKILL.md` resolving into it; one new test.

Result: **no Windows compatibility issue**, and the fix is verified on Windows with a junction.

The scenario is a checkout that contains `RAVEN_HOME`: the skill directory resolves inside the git boundary, so it passes the boundary check, and only the new `guarded` entry rejects it. The new unit test uses `_symlink_to` and therefore skips on this host (no symlink privilege), so I exercised the same resolved-target rule with a directory junction (`mklink /J`, creatable unelevated) against the head code:

```
junction workdir/.agents/skills/setup -> <repo>/.raven  (state_home contains SKILL.md)
project_skill_roots(..., state_home=state_home).guarded includes <repo>/.raven: True
read_project_skills(roots): ['kept']            # the junction target is not read
same roots with state_home removed from guarded (pre-fix shape): ['leaked']
```

The mutation (pre-fix guarded set) reads the `RAVEN_HOME` file, proving the new entry is what closes the leak on this platform, and a normal sibling skill is still collected.

Checks on this native Windows host, from the head tree (tarball checkout):

```
python -S runner.py tests/test_skill_forge_project_skills.py -q
-> 24 passed, 9 skipped   (the nine skips are the file's guarded symlink fixtures)
```

Gaps: tarball checkout; the new unit test itself is one of the nine skipped here, covered instead by the junction probe above.

## Windows compatibility review - PR #1390 @ 676bb8209f64106cbcd322680156d359a582102f

**Scope:** full PR diff against base 73005ee9f2 (2 files): `raven/memory_engine/skill_forge/project_skills.py` adds `RAVEN_HOME` (via `raven_home()`, with a `state_home` keyword) to `guarded`, and the test file gains a case plus the two-element `guarded[:2]` assertion.

**Result: no Windows compatibility issue found.** The guard is path-containment over resolved paths (`Path.is_relative_to`), which is platform-correct on Windows (`resolve()` here returns drive-letter paths and the comparison is case-sensitive on the normalized form, matching the existing guarded entries). No new separators, quoting, subprocess, encoding, or locking surface is introduced.

The new symlink test skips on this host (the suite's guarded `_symlink_to` reports Windows symlink privilege), so the Windows mechanism was re-verified with a directory junction at this head:

```
junction: repo/src/.agents/skills/setup -> repo/.raven/leak   (leak/SKILL.md valid)
guarded contains state_home: True
with guard: ['normal']
pre-fix guarded: ['...\\home\\.agents', '...\\agent-home']   (state_home removed)
pre-fix: ['normal', 'leaked']
```

The guard is load-bearing: without the `RAVEN_HOME` entry the junctioned `SKILL.md` is read as a project skill; with it, only the ordinary sibling is collected.

**Verification on this native Windows host** (Windows 11 26100; CPython from the shared venv; sparse partial clone pinned to 676bb8209f, paths `raven/`, `tests/`, `plugins-dist/`, `agents/`):

```
cd D:/tmp/g1390 && RVTREE='D:\tmp\g1390' PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=D:/tmp/pyc1390 PYTHONUTF8=1 \
  /d/projects/Raven/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -S /d/tmp/review-runner/runner.py \
  tests/test_skill_forge_project_skills.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
-> 30 passed, 13 skipped (final run; the 13 are the symlink-privilege skips)
```

Note for the author: the first full run had a single failure in `test_without_git_only_the_workdir_is_read`; it passed when run alone and in two subsequent full runs, so it is a non-reproducing flake on this host and not attributed to this PR.

**Gaps:** sparse partial clone rather than the whole repository; the real symlinked `SKILL.md` case cannot run here (Windows symlink privilege), so the junction probe stands in for it; no live skill index/BM25 run.
